title: Hippocampal and Entorhinal Neurons
intro: The hippocampus and the entorhinal cortex next to it form the brain's system for episodic memory and spatial navigation. Their neurons are where place cells and grid cells were discovered, and their simple, layered anatomy made them the first brain region whose cell types were modelled in detail. For a builder of cortical columns they matter twice: as the source of the location codes that the Thousand Brains Theory borrows, and as a model of how a few cell types implement pattern separation and pattern completion.

blocks.text: Input arrives from layer 2 of the entorhinal cortex (EC) through the perforant path to the dentate gyrus (DG), whose granule cells project through mossy fibres to CA3. CA3 pyramidal cells connect strongly to each other (the recurrent collaterals) and project through Schaffer collaterals to CA1. CA1 also receives direct input from entorhinal layer 3, and sends the output back to entorhinal layer 5 and to the subiculum. This is the 'trisynaptic loop' EC → DG → CA3 → CA1, plus the direct EC → CA1 path. Around these principal cells, more than 20 types of interneuron (Freund & Buzsaki 1996; Klausberger & Somogyi 2008) control timing relative to the theta (4 to 12 Hz) and sharp-wave ripple (about 150 to 250 Hz) rhythms.

 Classic computational roles (Marr 1971; McNaughton & Morris 1987; Treves & Rolls 1994):
   DG   pattern separation   sparse, expanded code, few active granule cells
   CA3  pattern completion   autoassociative memory via recurrent collaterals
   CA1  comparison / output  matches CA3 recall against direct EC input

items: CA1 Pyramidal Cells (#/neuroscience/cell-types/hippocampal/ca1-pyramidal): place cells, dendritic plateaus and behavioural timescale plasticity, the Poirazi two-layer model.
CA3 Pyramidal Cells (#/neuroscience/cell-types/hippocampal/ca3-pyramidal): intrinsic bursting, recurrent autoassociation, the Pinsky-Rinzel and Traub models.
Dentate Granule Cells (#/neuroscience/cell-types/hippocampal/dentate-granule): extremely sparse firing, adult neurogenesis, pattern separation.
OLM Interneurons (#/neuroscience/cell-types/hippocampal/olm-interneuron): slow, dendrite-targeting interneurons that pace theta.
Entorhinal Stellate Cells (#/neuroscience/cell-types/hippocampal/mec-stellate): grid cells, theta resonance and the h-current.

blocks.text: Why the hippocampus is a good modelling lab

items: Its principal cells form tidy layers, so recordings, morphologies and dendritic measurements are abundant.
Its cell types are catalogued in detail: Hippocampome.org lists over 120 types with markers, morphologies and fitted Izhikevich parameters.

There are full-scale models: Bezaire et al. (2016) simulated a full-scale rat CA1 with 338,740 cells of nine types and reproduced theta and gamma; Blue Brain's CA1 model (Romani et al. 2024) reconstructs a full rat CA1 region.
Its theories connect cell types to computation directly: the dentate gyrus, CA3 and CA1 each have a well-defined proposed role that a model can test.
